author: enumeration_review
standing: Transitive connected string C-group in A_n, all maximal omissions intransitive.
G0 has singleton a and its complementary orbit; rho0=(a b)delta.
claims: Transport to paired points of a natural or other self-centralizing R-orbit consumes two equal orbit copies and gives an independent-image length bound.

If the exact nonidentity actions on even fixed set F are its f-1 successive path transpositions, the block begins at rho2; rho1 fixes the remaining f-1 F vertices and sends the first into an R-fixed delta-pair.
Under this literal natural fixed-path hypothesis, f=6 is impossible, including t=3 and no remaining pair-only labels.
proof_branches: M pair images inherit orbit-essentiality by adjoining the other distinguished labels to orbit-equivalent omissions.
An odd centralizing involution forbids pair transitivity; the m-2 forest forces exactly two full pair orbits.
Saturated cuts force exact pair transpositions and S_A times S_B.
Parity forces two odd-sized pair orbits and individual complete flips; the middle label support is then preserved by all of G0.
not_claimed: The five natural path restrictions do not follow here from arbitrary transitivity on six fixed points.
General f>=6 and arbitrary fixed-set actions, exceptional heads, connected-square rigidity and remaining original tables remain pending.
